newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SOCCER-SWEDEN BRING IN NEW CAP FOR SCOTLAND MATCH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SWEDEN BRING IN NEW CAP FOR SCOTLAND MATCH.

text.p: Sweden, struggling to qualify for the 1998 World Cup finals, on Tuesday introduced one new cap to face Scotland next month in a match that could also decide the fate of manager Tommy Svensson.

Pressure is growing on Svensson following a lacklustre 1-0 defeat against Austria earlier this month that raised the prospect of Sweden missing out on the World Cup finals after failing to qualify for this year's European Championships.
Sweden were beaten semifinalists in the 1994 World Cup.
A leading Swedish daily, Dagens Nyheter, this week called on Svensson to resign if Sweden lose in Glasgow.
But Svensson rejected such calls, telling reporters on Tuesday: "As long as we have a chance to qualify for the finals then I have no reason to think along such lines."

Svensson dropped Bari midfielder Klas Ingesson for the November 10 match, replacing him with Gothenburg's Niclas Alexandersson, who received the news as he trained with Gothenburg in Italy ahead of Wednesday's match against AC Milan.

Svensson said striker Martin Dahlin, who is set to play top class football again this weekend for Germany's Borussia Munchengladbach after leaving Italy's Roma, where he was relegated to the substitute's bench, would probably not play a full match for Sweden against Scotland.
Defence: Patrik Andersson (Borussia Munchengladbach), Joachim Bjorklund (Glasgow Rangers), Teddy Lucic (Gothenburg), Jozo Matovac (Orgryte), Roland Nilsson (Helsingborg), Gary Sundgren (AIK).
Midfield: Niclas Alexandersson, (Gothenburg), Jesper Blomqvist (Gothenburg), Hakan Mild (Real Sociedad), Stefan Schwarz (Fiorentina), Jonas Thern (Roma), Par Zetterberg (Anderlecht).
Attack: Andreas Andersson, (Gothenburg), Kennet Andersson, (Bologna), Martin Dahlin, (Borussia Munchengladbach), Henrik Larsson (Feyenoord).
